item.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
item.description: The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups. The flaw is in builds that use the OpenSSL backend with mutual-TLS, where the server checks a client certificate and vice versa, and a revocation list is configured to block revoked…

item.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
item.description: Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file. Patches for the flaw were released last month by Apple in…

item.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
item.description: Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account. item.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
item.description: Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing.
